standing: Independently prepared fresh confirmation for C1 (named-document, resolved-family scope). Engineering corpus dolved-care-v4 checkpoint-19, primary scope. Not held-out; not a statistically independent reliability estimate. No family here appears in block1-* evidence or apps test fixtures (grep at authoring time). Families excluded at authoring: those used in the temporal package, input 16, checkpoint inputs (pressure area, gas safety, resident finances, DoLS, uniform allowance, e-learning, on-call manager, key cutting, learning from deaths), and three 'added_removed_clause' families whose v2 claims removal of a permission v1 never states (agency staff usage, software licensing, pet visiting) - recorded as a corpus observation, not fixed.
source_basis: Authored from semantic masters; key sentences confirmed verbatim in the rendered .txt artefacts for F1, F4, F5 and artefact SHA-256 prefixes match source-manifest for the PDF families (F2, F3). PDF text and ALL items must be verified against the ingested authorised chunks and the production DocumentAuthorityTimeline before execution; that verification happens only after C1 is frozen, and any defect is recorded and resolved explicitly, never silently edited.

verdict_rules.answer: Existing stage-specific rule: correct / qualified-correct / wrong / no-answer / clarification. Wrong = misstates source, wrong version or period, omits an explicitly requested part, drops a gating source condition, or asserts more than the source supports.
verdict_rules.route: Record per item whether the requested-history route or the new precautionary C1 route produced the evidence, whether the alternative lane and slot were preserved, and the validated answer target. A correct answer via the existing requested-history route is NOT evidence that the C1 safeguard executed.
verdict_rules.c1_holds: Wrong-version answer from the new mechanism; historical precautionary evidence used as direct support for a current claim; unsafe target promotion; silent loss of a required target; any permission/authority/citation violation.

items.expected_answer: Within 4 hours of the complaint being received, regardless of the time of day (the version in force on 10 March 2026). Mentioning that the window is now 2 hours is acceptable if clearly labelled as the later rule.
items.source_support: v1: 'Escalate a serious complaint to the Quality Lead within 4 hours of it being received, regardless of the time of day.' v2: 'within 2 hours of it being received, a tightening from the previous 4-hour window'.
items.wrong: 2 hours presented as the rule on 10 March 2026; or no-answer when v1 is eligible.

items.versions: v1 effective 2025-02-01, superseded 2026-02-01 (in force March 2025; no capacity-screen requirement); v2 effective 2026-02-01 (current, selected).
items.expected_answer: Yes. The current policy requires a documented mental capacity screen as part of every pre-admission assessment (a new mandatory step). Under the emergency placement route the screen may be completed within the first 72 hours of admission; mentioning this is good but not required.
items.source_support: v2: 'Complete a documented mental capacity screen as part of every pre-admission assessment, a new mandatory step introduced in this version.' v2: under the emergency placement route '... the fuller assessment, GP summary and mental capacity screen completed within the first 72 hours of admission.'
items.wrong: Answering from v1 (no screen required / not mentioned) because of the March 2025 admission; presenting historical evidence as the current requirement; asserting the screen must always precede admission with no emergency allowance.
